title: Write one launch brief as prompts and settings for four different image models, and mark which outputs need a human check
scenario:
A lighting brand launches a desk lamp called Lumen. Your teammate turned one brief into prompts and settings for four image models, and marked which outputs need a human check. You review the plan before the first request.

Use the exhibit. The brand, the files and the plan are made up for this case. The model names, fields and licences are from the vendors' docs in October 2026.
exhibit:
BRIEF (made up):
  Lumen desk lamp launch. One hero poster, a set of web
  images in one look, and a desk scene without people or clutter.
  Headline on the poster: LUMEN
  Brand yellow: #F2B705
  Two approved product photos: lamp-a.png, lamp-b.png
  The brand owns both photos.

PLAN (draft, made up):
  Model 1  Ideogram 4.5 (Image app)
           Prompt:   "A brass desk lamp on an oak desk, warm evening light"
           Negative prompt field: "people, clutter"
           Human check: no

  Model 2  FLUX 3 Image (BFL API)
           Layout element: { "id": "title", "bbox": [60, 100, 220, 900],
             "desc": "the word \"LUMEN\" in bold yellow capitals" }
           "seed": 777   (so we can make the poster again later)
           Human check: no, the box fixes the headline

  Model 3  Recraft V4.1 (API)
           Step 1: train a custom model on lamp-a.png and lamp-b.png
           Step 2: wait for training, then send its style_id with
                   each web image request
           Human check: colour only

  Model 4  FLUX.2 [klein] 4B Base
           Train a small LoRA on the two photos, then call the
           Base model through BFL's public API with the LoRA
           Human check: yes

questions.prompt: Model 1 uses a negative prompt field on Ideogram 4.5. What should change?

options.text: Keep the field; on Ideogram 4.5 it always wins over the main prompt
options.explanation: Only Ideogram 3.0 has a separate Negative prompt field, and there Ideogram says the main prompt always wins.

options.text: Drop the field and describe what you want, such as an empty, clear desk
options.explanation: Right. Only Ideogram 3.0 has a separate Negative prompt field. Ideogram says "An empty street" works better than "a street with no people".

options.text: Move "people, clutter" to a --no flag at the end of the main prompt
options.explanation: Ideogram does not read flags as commands. It treats them as words, which it may try to draw.

options.text: Write "NO PEOPLE, NO CLUTTER" in capitals at the start of the prompt
options.explanation: These are still negatives. Ideogram's guide prefers saying what you want to see.

questions.prompt: Model 2 marks the poster "no human check" because a box places the headline. What is right?

options.text: The box is enough, because a layout box fixes the spelling of the words
options.explanation: A box places text. It does not spell it. Every letter still needs reading.

options.text: Only Ideogram output needs a check, because FLUX never misspells text
options.explanation: Every model here can get text wrong. The guides say to check the words in the output.

options.text: A check is needed only if the box numbers list x before y
options.explanation: Box order decides where the text lands, not whether it is spelled right.

options.text: Mark it yes: a box places the text but doesn't spell it; read every letter
options.explanation: Right. Boxes place text; they don't spell it. Any output with words in it needs a proof-read.

questions.prompt: Model 2 also sends "seed": 777 to FLUX 3 Image. What happens?

options.text: FLUX 3 Image rejects unknown fields like seed with an HTTP 422 error
options.explanation: Right. BFL says the FLUX 3 Image endpoint rejects unknown fields with HTTP 422, so fields such as seed don't work there.

options.text: The seed works, and the same seed repeats the poster pixel for pixel
options.explanation: FLUX 3 Image takes no seed. And even where seeds work, they give the same or a very close result, not a promise.

options.text: FLUX 3 Image ignores the seed quietly and makes a random poster
options.explanation: BFL says the endpoint rejects unknown fields with HTTP 422. It does not ignore them.

options.text: The seed works only if the prompt is also set to the same 777 words
options.explanation: No source ties a seed to the prompt length. FLUX 3 Image takes no seed at all.

questions.prompt: Model 3 trains a model before it can use the two photos. What is the better plan on Recraft?

options.text: Keep the training job, since only a trained model can reuse one look
options.explanation: Recraft returns a style_id from reference images, and later requests can reuse it. No training is needed.

options.text: Attach both photos as style references now, then reuse the style_id
options.explanation: Right. Recraft builds a V4 style from references with no training, and returns a style_id that later requests can reuse.

options.text: Skip the photos and set match to precise, which needs no reference
options.explanation: match is a setting of a style. The style itself still comes from your reference images.

options.text: Send the photos and an old style_id together, for a stronger match
options.explanation: Recraft rejects a request with both a style_id and style references.

questions.prompt: Model 4 calls FLUX.2 [klein] 4B Base through BFL's public API. What is the problem?

options.text: Base models are not on BFL's public API; download and run it yourself
options.explanation: Right. BFL says the Base models are open weights for local use and are not offered on the public API.

options.text: The 4B Base is non-commercial, so the brand cannot use it at all
options.explanation: BFL lists [klein] 4B and 4B Base under Apache 2.0. The 9B versions are the non-commercial ones.

options.text: A LoRA can't be trained on a Base model, only on the API models
options.explanation: BFL says the Base models are for fine-tuning, LoRA training, research and custom pipelines.

options.text: Nothing: every FLUX.2 model, Base included, is on the public API
options.explanation: BFL says the Base models are not offered on the public API.
